What one hundred thousand, three hundred is my price!
Fine, we meet in an hour in the back courtyard.

Hello, Timur, hi, how do I settle a conflict?

Well, there are always two options here.
The second option is really costly.
There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.
Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?
Yes, bring good meat and good wine.
Wait, I wanted everything to go peacefully.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Максим, тебя там с седьмого столика зовут.
examples.trans: Maxim, they are calling for you from Table Seven.

examples.text: Хорошо, только у меня там блюдо на кухне.
examples.trans: Alright, only I have a dish in the kitchen.

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ляна'). Common feminine noun meaning 'table / feast (slang)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

examples.text: Потому что это наша поляна!
examples.trans: Because this is our turf!

examples.text: В лесу мы вышли на солнечную поляну.
examples.trans: In the forest we came out onto a sunny clearing.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Тебе надо дыхание надолго задержать.
examples.trans: You need to hold your breath for a long time.

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

examples.text: Слушай, надо что-то с этим делать!
examples.trans: Listen, we have to do something about this!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'крывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to set / lay (a table)'.

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и накрывать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to set on time.

meanings.en: to treat someone to food or drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'гощать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to treat / host', paired with 'угостить'.

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

examples.text: Хорошо, посидим вечером, я угощаю!
examples.trans: Alright, we will sit together tonight, my treat!

examples.text: Почему мы должны угощать кого-то?
examples.trans: Why should we treat anyone?

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Господи, какой же ты всё-таки жалкий!
examples.trans: Good Lord, how pathetic you really are!

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

examples.text: Поэтому я от души благословляю вас.
examples.trans: Therefore I bless you from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Ты уберёшь свою машину прямо сейчас, понял?
examples.trans: You are going to move your car right now, got it?

examples.text: Понял, а сколько здесь денег?
examples.trans: Got it, and how much money is here?

examples.text: Понял, ты думаешь, сразу нести шашлык?
examples.trans: Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'think, suppose', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Я подумал, что Катя такая красивая и хорошая.
examples.trans: I thought that Katya is so beautiful and good.

examples.text: Понял, ты думаешь, сразу нести шашлык?
examples.trans: Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?

examples.text: Только если у него инфаркт будет, это ты придумал.
examples.trans: Only if he has a heart attack, you came up with it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.text: Я его сейчас дофарширую и сразу выйду.
examples.trans: I will finish stuffing it right now and come right out.

examples.text: Понял, ты думаешь, сразу нести шашлык?
examples.trans: Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?

examples.text: Сейчас я там дофарширую и сразу приду.
examples.trans: I will finish stuffing it in there right now and come right back.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring, carry', paired with 'понести'.

examples.text: Лёва, но это же несправедливо!
examples.trans: Lyova, but that is unfair!

examples.text: Понял, ты думаешь, сразу нести шашлык?
examples.trans: Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?

examples.text: Да, неси хорошее мясо и вино хорошее.
examples.trans: Yes, bring good meat and good wine.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'shashlik / skewered meat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Понял, ты думаешь, сразу нести шашлык?
examples.trans: Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки!
examples.trans: Let's drive out to the forest for shashlik!

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки! Даню вон с собой возьмём.
examples.trans: Let's drive out to the forest for shashlik! We will take Danya here along with us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дам тебе покататься, спасибо, зайду.
examples.trans: I will let you go for a ride, thanks, I will stop by.

examples.text: Девчонки меня так недавно назвали.
examples.trans: The girls recently gave me that name.

examples.text: Лёва, пожалуйста, даже не начинай.
examples.trans: Lyova, please, do not even start.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'meat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да, неси хорошее мясо и вино хорошее.
examples.trans: Yes, bring good meat and good wine.

examples.text: Неси мясо и вино хорошее.
examples.trans: Bring good meat and good wine.

examples.text: Скажи, а что это за мясо?
examples.trans: Tell me, what kind of meat is this?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да, неси хорошее мясо и вино хорошее.
examples.trans: Yes, bring good meat and good wine.

examples.text: Хочу вам предложить хорошее блюдо с хорошим вином.
examples.trans: I want to offer you a good dish with good wine.

examples.text: Неси мясо и вино хорошее.
examples.trans: Bring good meat and good wine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Подождите, я хотел, чтобы всё прошло мирно.
examples.trans: Wait, I wanted everything to go peacefully.

examples.text: Катя, не слушай его, он хотел получить деньги!
examples.trans: Katya, do not listen to him, he wanted to get money!

examples.text: Да я трогать его не хотел, он меня спровоцировал!
examples.trans: I did not want to touch him, he provoked me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что у тебя за мастерская?
examples.trans: And what kind of workshop do you have?

examples.text: Вы что, знакомы, это мой отец!
examples.trans: Do you two know each other, this is my father!

examples.text: Привет, что ты мне названиваешь?
examples.trans: Hi, why do you keep calling me?

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go through, to pass; to come along', paired with 'проходить'.

related.gloss: not to to go through (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Пройдите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Go through, please.

examples.text: Потом пройдёт.
examples.trans: Then it passes.

examples.text: Неужели нельзя, чтобы день прошёл нормально?
examples.trans: Can a day really not pass normally?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Подождите, я хотел, чтобы всё прошло мирно.
examples.trans: Wait, I wanted everything to go peacefully.

examples.text: Парни, давайте мы всё миром решим.
examples.trans: Guys, let's settle everything peacefully.

examples.text: Давайте всё миром решим.
examples.trans: Let's settle everything peacefully.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы что, знакомы, это мой отец!
examples.trans: Do you two know each other, this is my father!

examples.text: А за моржа весь день мусор выносишь.
examples.trans: And for the walrus comment, you are taking out the trash all day.

examples.text: Ну тогда пойдём выйдем, приляжешь.
examples.trans: Well then let's step outside and you can lie down.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offer', paired with 'предлагать'.

examples.text: Хочу вам предложить хорошее блюдо с хорошим вином.
examples.trans: I want to offer you a good dish with good wine.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу.
examples.trans: But you were offered a job.

examples.text: Он предложил кофе.
examples.trans: He offered coffee.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хорошо, только у меня там блюдо на кухне.
examples.trans: Alright, only I have a dish in the kitchen.

examples.text: Хочу вам предложить хорошее блюдо с хорошим вином.
examples.trans: I want to offer you a good dish with good wine.

examples.text: Ой, я перепутал, это блюдо не вам!
examples.trans: Oops, I mixed it up, this dish is not for you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Двести лошадей, отличный мотоцикл!
examples.trans: Two hundred horsepower, an excellent motorcycle!

examples.text: У меня в молодости такой мотоцикл был.
examples.trans: I had a motorcycle like that in my youth.

examples.text: Час гоняешь, потом весь день перебираешь.
examples.trans: You ride for an hour, then overhaul it all day.
